sentences.text: 1. Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.870/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act registered at police station Begumpur, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 23.11.2015 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.

However, due to matrimonial discord,
the couple started living separately from each other since the year 2016 and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter in the year 2017 and started living under one roof in the matrimonial home of respondent No.2.
On 04.12.2017, the couple was blessed with a boy namely Kanishk and they are living happily as husband and wife.
Again on 15.11.2021 the written settlement agreement was executed between the This is a digitally signed order.

The respondent No.2 does not wish to pursue her case against the petitioners in the interest of her matrimonial home and in the interest of her family.

3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no Sahil & Ors vs State Through Sho Ps Begum Pur & Anr on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101170844/
1 objection if the FIR is quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.
4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes with the petitioners.
She has already joined the matrimonial home and both are living happily.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, FIR No.870/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act registered at police station Begumpur, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
MAY 17, 2023 M
